themes.name: AI compute: NVIDIA's supply chain
themes.what: Commerce released a rule on Nov 16 that requires a license for advanced AI chips sent to any data center, anywhere, that serves China linked firms at scale, and adds license needs for Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil; US headquartered buyers are exempt if they report monthly (Traders and Quants). It is expected to take effect Thursday. The chip index fell 5.3% Monday; NVDA closed 156.14 (-4.12%), TSM 373.45 (-6.34%), MU 719.02 (-7.62%) and DELL 320.55 (-6.96%) (Massive). Hours before its report, Nvidia's board set up a national security and export compliance committee (Traders and Quants).
themes.for_you: The rule starts after Nvidia gives its next outlook, so a slow license in the five countries would land on a number already given. No first tranche in AI names before tonight's report. ANET and ADI stay on the long term scan buy list, but wait for the reaction.

themes.name: AI power and the grid
themes.what: Powell Industries rose 5.94% to 151.20 on Nov 16 on about 4 times normal volume while chips fell, then reported after the close: backlog nearly doubled from a year earlier to $2.7 billion, with a $250 million LNG order and an $85 million data center order (Traders and Quants; Massive). The close cleared the box POWL built after its Nov 5 drop.
themes.for_you: A confirmed break up after a big drop, but the dashboard reads it as a bounce inside a downtrend (lower highs and lower lows, under the 200 day). A reason to check the chart, not a buy. No swing setup or put here.
